newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks hit 31-month high.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks hit 31-month high.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks built on Monday's near 200-point climb to close at their highest level in 31 months on Tuesday, buoyed by Wall Street's record highs and the view that a near-term rate rise would not hit stocks hard.
Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index closed up 53.71 points, or 0.46 percent, at 11,621.61, off an intra-day high of 11,645.35.
This was the highest level since a 12,157.57 close on February 4, 1994.

However, while some brokers saw positive changes in the market's underlying fundamentals, others were cautious on the near-term outlook for the market, citing futures-related buying and an over-dependence on U.S. trends as negative factors.
"There were probably more buy orders to be filled in the market today than yesterday, with decent two-way trade in a narrow range," said Glenn Lesko, head of equities trading at HG Asia.
"We saw some resistance at the 11,600 level, but the cash market was quite buoyant," Lesko said.

"With precious little news on the domestic front, Hong Kong remains tied to the U.S. interest rate outlook -- which now looks limited to a 0.25 percent hike," said James Osborn, sales director at ING Barings.

The U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meets on September 24 and many Fed watchers are predicting a 25-basis-point rise in short-term rates following a series of subdued reports on inflation and retail sales.
"The index's hesitation at 11,600 -- the previous 1996 intra-day high -- suggests investors are confused about the correct valuation for the market," Osborn said.
"We are still waiting to see how institutional funds will reallocate their Asian funds."
Turnover on Tuesday was a healthy HK$7.05 billion ($912.03 million), just shy of Monday's HK$7.56 billion, and brokers cited the rise in turnover as the single most bullish factor in the market.
"Average turnover over the past few months has been less than HK$4 billion and this breakthrough is very positive," said David Williamson, sales director at UBS Securities (East Asia) Ltd.
"I also do not believe that funds are overweighted in this market. I think Asian strategists are likely to increase their weightings in Hong Kong in the fourth quarter," he said.
Some analysts warned that buying activity had been padded by the futures-related buying of hedge funds.
"The quality of buying was not great, not institutional and this is the reason for the market's intra-day volatility," said Conal Sanjana, institutional sales manager at Kerry Securities.
September index futures, which traded on a near-par with the cash index at midday, closed at a 30-point discount to the cash market.
